The International Civil Aviation Organization (2025) maintains a list of current offtake agreements that highlights the potential size of the market and committed airlines. General aviation also enters into offtake agreements. 2.4.1 Consumption, Plants, and Capacity EIA does not publish SAF data; therefore, the best approximation of SAF volumes is derived from EPA’s RIN data. As evidenced in Figure 8, SAF production increases each year. This trend is expected to continue with new domestic plants starting up in late 2024 and spring 2025. Figure 9 shows the high variability of monthly SAF RIN generation, which may represent market dynamics of plants producing both SAF and renewable diesel and potentially competition for 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. foreign SAF in the United States (Neste 2022). Figure 9 extends into 2025 to highlight a significant shift to consumption of domestically produced SAF. Despite increased production, SAF represents a tiny fraction of the overall U.S. jet fuel market of 26 billion gallons in 2024 (EIA 2025m). In 2024, there were five domestic commercial plants and one international producer supplying the U.S. market. Three of the plants are conversions of refineries—World Energy, Montana Renewables, and Phillips 66—while Diamond Green Diesel and New Rise Renewables are new plants. Neste, an international producer, has plants in Finland, the Netherlands, and Singapore. Neste exports to the United States, and their production capacity was 515 million gallons (34,000 barrels/day) as of May 2025 (Neste 2025). Section 2.5.1 of this report details renewable diesel producers. While most of those plants do not produce SAF today, they have the potential to do so if market conditions are favorable.
